pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: src/__tests__/lib/state-machine-compile.test.ts:116 The exported C++ is checked only by regex and substring, with no compiler or C++ parser reading it in any lane I could find, so code the compiler would reject can pass while the test restates one compiler rule by hand.

techniques.evidence: src/__tests__/lib/state-machine-compile.test.ts:116 generateFullCppOutput is referenced only by its test, the editor hook and a re-export; package.json has no clang or tree-sitter, and compiling is left to the model session via the applyPlan.ts:201 prompt line. Caveat: the real reader is the local UE toolchain, which is not unit-cost, so the technique's 'reader not available in the lane' exclusion is arguable, but no cost estimate or syntax-only check is recorded.
src/__tests__/components/animations/state-machine-editor-wiring.test.tsx:56 The test enters through the shipped parent view and opens the real tab, rather than composing the editor itself.
src/__tests__/lib/state-machine-compile.test.ts:60 Beside the 'false finding is gone' absences, the exact findings from the compiled entry are asserted, so a check that stopped running would go red.

src/__tests__/lib/state-machine-compile.test.ts:38 The golden is a hand-held source constant with no record mode, and no toMatchSnapshot appears in this context's tests, so there is no update path to guard.

pairs.registryProposal: assert-through-the-reader's 'reader is not available in the lane' exclusion does not cover a reader that is installed locally but takes minutes and needs a whole engine, such as a UE C++ build. The technique could say whether a syntax-only parse against stub headers satisfies it, or whether the claim moves to a scheduled lane.

pairs.registryProposal: pin-the-call-not-the-name's population section covers floors on walks but not a hand-written file list narrower than the rule the pin states. That shape has an implicit floor, since a missing file throws, and still fails toward green.
